---
title: "Niger - Millet: the date is the decision"
subtitle: "Thirty-three rainy seasons around Niamey and Sadoré, eight sowing dates: when pearl millet goes into the ground matters more than whether it gets fertiliser"
---

```{ojs}
import {withDownload, cellFeatures, fmt, locatorMap, placeMarks, boxPolygon} from "../assets/js/dl.js"
S = FileAttachment("data/niger/summary.json").json()
B = FileAttachment("data/niger/boundaries.json").json()
countries = FileAttachment("data/niger/countries.geojson").json()
adm1 = FileAttachment("data/niger/adm1.geojson").json()
adm2 = FileAttachment("data/niger/adm2.geojson").json()
dates = FileAttachment("data/niger/dates.csv").csv({typed: true})
years = FileAttachment("data/niger/years.csv").csv({typed: true})
bestYear = FileAttachment("data/niger/best_date_per_year.csv").csv({typed: true})
bestCell = FileAttachment("data/niger/best_date_per_cell.csv").csv({typed: true})
sowLabel = d => new Date(2001, 5, 1 + d).toLocaleDateString("en-GB", {day: "numeric", month: "short"})
sowDays = [...new Set(dates.map(d => d.sow_day))].sort((a, b) => a - b)
nColor = ({domain: ["0 kg N", "45 kg N"], range: ["#c98b2b", "#2b6cb0"]})
d45 = dates.filter(d => d.n === 45)
d0 = dates.filter(d => d.n === 0)
top = d45.reduce((a, b) => (b.mean > a.mean ? b : a))
first = d45.find(d => d.sow_day === 0)
```

| Setup | |
|---|---|
| Area | 2.0-3.0 E, 13.0-14.0 N, around Niamey and the ICRISAT Sahelian Centre at Sadoré (13.28 N, 2.00 E in the experiment's weather file) |
| Crop map | MapSPAM 2020 pearl millet, physical area [@spam2020] |
| Weather, soil | AgERA5 1990-2024 [@agera5]; SoilGrids 2.0 [@poggio2021], one profile per 0.1° cell |
| Crop, template | CERES-Millet, cultivar CIVT, 3 plants/m², from the Sadoré experiment ITSC8601 (1986) |
| Treatments | rainfed; 0 or 45 kg N/ha (the experiment's own levels) |
| Sowing | 1 June to 10 August, every 10 days, the same date in every cell and year |
| Years | 1991-2023, 33 rainy seasons |
| Boundaries | edge-matched OCHA administrative boundaries (COD-AB) from HDX: [Niger](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-ner) (IGNN and OCHA/ROWCA; licence listed as "other"), [Benin](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-ben), [Burkina Faso](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-bfa), [Nigeria](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-nga) (CC BY-IGO) |
| Experiment file | [`configs/cases/niger-millet.yml`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/xdssat/blob/main/configs/cases/niger-millet.yml) |

## Eight dates, one crop

In the Sahel the rains set the season, and one decision is left to whoever farms the field: the day to sow.
This page asks the crop model a single question. The same pearl millet, in the same fields, with the same
soil and the same fertiliser, is sown on eight different days. How much does the date alone change the
harvest? The switch below sets the nitrogen rate for every chart on the page.

```{ojs}
viewof nPick = Inputs.radio(new Map([["0 kg N/ha", 0], ["45 kg N/ha", 45]]), {value: 45, label: "Nitrogen"})
dN = dates.filter(d => d.n === nPick)
topN = dN.reduce((a, b) => (b.mean > a.mean ? b : a))
firstN = dN.find(d => d.sow_day === 0)
```

```{ojs}
md`Averaged over 33 seasons, millet sown on **${sowLabel(topN.sow_day)}** gives the most grain:
**${fmt.int(topN.mean)} kg/ha** with ${nPick} kg N. Sown on **1 June** the same crop gives **${fmt.int(firstN.mean)} kg/ha**,
${fmt.d1(topN.mean / firstN.mean)} times less. The band shows the spread over the years: in nine years out of ten the
yield of a date lies above its lower edge, in one out of ten above its upper edge.`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 340, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Sowing date", tickFormat: sowLabel, ticks: sowDays},
  y: {label: "Grain yield, kg/ha (area-weighted, dry matter)", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, ...nColor},
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY(dN, {x: "sow_day", y1: "p10", y2: "p90", fill: nPick === 45 ? "#2b6cb0" : "#c98b2b", fillOpacity: 0.15}),
    Plot.areaY(dN, {x: "sow_day", y1: "p25", y2: "p75", fill: nPick === 45 ? "#2b6cb0" : "#c98b2b", fillOpacity: 0.2}),
    Plot.line(d45, {x: "sow_day", y: "mean", stroke: () => "45 kg N", strokeWidth: nPick === 45 ? 2.5 : 1.2}),
    Plot.line(d0, {x: "sow_day", y: "mean", stroke: () => "0 kg N", strokeWidth: nPick === 0 ? 2.5 : 1.2, strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.dot(dN, {x: "sow_day", y: "mean", fill: nPick === 45 ? "#2b6cb0" : "#c98b2b", r: 4}),
    Plot.ruleX(dN, Plot.pointerX({x: "sow_day", stroke: "#999", strokeDasharray: "2,2"})),
    Plot.tip(dN, Plot.pointerX({x: "sow_day", y: "mean",
      title: d => `Sown ${sowLabel(d.sow_day)}, ${d.n} kg N\nmean ${fmt.int(d.mean)} kg/ha\nmedian ${fmt.int(d.p50)}\n` +
        `10th-90th percentile ${fmt.int(d.p10)}-${fmt.int(d.p90)}\nseason rain ${fmt.int(d.rain_mean)} mm`})),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), "niger_yield_by_sowing_date", "line: mean of 33 seasons; bands: 25th-75th and 10th-90th percentile of the chosen N rate")
```

## A June shower is a trap

Why does an early crop fail? Not because it dies. Every one of the 69,696 simulated seasons ends with a crop
"harvested at maturity" (the engine's crop status 1); none fails to germinate, none is killed by drought.
The early crop fails slowly. Pearl millet develops on heat: its clock runs on temperature, not on water.
Sown on 1 June it emerges in about five days, flowers after about 33 and is mature after about 75, as a July
crop would. But it lives those days before the rains have settled. It catches a median 147 mm of rain from
sowing to harvest, against 233 mm for a crop sown on 11 July, builds almost no leaf (a largest leaf area
index of 0.0, against 2.1) and only 95 kg/ha of biomass (45 kg N).

A drier start does not save it. CERES-Millet holds a seed back only while the soil at seed depth is at its
lower limit of plant-available water (`ML_PHENOL.for:415-421`, DSSAT-CSM 4.8). This case starts every season
at 30% of the available water, so seeds germinate at once. **Tested** on 20 cells, 1991-2023, 45 kg N: with
the soil at its lower limit at the start, a 1 June seed waits a median 7 days (90th percentile 21, longest
52) and emerges around 8 June, on the first shower that wets the seed layer, then grows into the dry spells
that follow. Yield: 63 kg/ha (1 June) and 822 kg/ha (11 July), against 74 and 973 kg/ha with the moister
start. The early shower is a false start.

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 260, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Sowing date", tickFormat: sowLabel, type: "band"},
  y: {label: "Rain, sowing to harvest (mm)", grid: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(dN, {x: "sow_day", y: "rain_mean", fill: "#4a90a4", inset: 6, tip: true,
      title: d => `Sown ${sowLabel(d.sow_day)}\nmean season rain ${fmt.int(d.rain_mean)} mm\nmean yield ${fmt.int(d.mean)} kg/ha`}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), "niger_rain_by_sowing_date", "mean over 33 seasons and all cells, area-weighted")
```

## Every year draws its own best date

```{ojs}
bestN = bestYear.filter(d => d.n === nPick)
bestCounts = d3.rollups(bestN, v => v.length, d => d.sow_day).sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0])
md`The best date is not the same every year. Over the 33 seasons the best of the eight dates (${nPick} kg N) was
${bestCounts.map(([d, k]) => `**${sowLabel(d)}** in ${k} year${k > 1 ? "s" : ""}`).join(", ")}.
Each row below is one rainy season; the darker a square, the more grain that date gave that year, and the dot
marks the year's best date. Pick a year to see its curve against the 33-season mean.`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 620, marginLeft: 45, padding: 0,
  x: {label: "Sowing date", tickFormat: sowLabel, type: "band"},
  y: {label: null, type: "band", reverse: true, tickFormat: String},
  color: {scheme: "YlGnBu", legend: true, label: `Grain yield, kg/ha (${nPick} kg N)`},
  marks: [
    Plot.cell(years.filter(d => d.n === nPick), {x: "sow_day", y: "year", fill: "yield", inset: 0.5, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.year}, sown ${sowLabel(d.sow_day)}\n${fmt.int(d.yield)} kg/ha\n${fmt.int(d.rain)} mm rain, sowing to harvest`}),
    Plot.dot(bestN, {x: "sow_day", y: "year", fill: "white", stroke: "#222", r: 3.5}),
    Plot.cell(years.filter(d => d.n === nPick && d.year === yearPick), {x: "sow_day", y: "year", fill: "none",
      stroke: "#d0021b", strokeWidth: 2})
  ]
}), "niger_years_by_date", "area-weighted mean of 132 cells per season; dot: best date of the year; red: the picked year")
```

```{ojs}
viewof yearPick = Inputs.select([...new Set(years.map(d => d.year))].sort(), {value: 1998, label: "Year", format: String})
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 260, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Sowing date", tickFormat: sowLabel, ticks: sowDays},
  y: {label: "Grain yield, kg/ha", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: [String(yearPick), "mean of 33 seasons"], range: ["#d0021b", "#888"]},

    Plot.dot(years.filter(d => d.n === nPick && d.year === yearPick), {x: "sow_day", y: "yield", fill: "#d0021b", tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.year}, sown ${sowLabel(d.sow_day)}\n${fmt.int(d.yield)} kg/ha, ${fmt.int(d.rain)} mm rain`}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), `niger_year_${yearPick}`, `one season (${nPick} kg N) against the 33-season mean`)
```

## The cost of a wrong date is a bad year

The mean hides the risk. A field is harvested one season at a time, not on average. The share of seasons in
which a date gives less than a threshold tells the risk of each date; move the threshold to see how the
ranking holds.

```{ojs}
viewof poor = Inputs.range([100, 1000], {value: 300, step: 50, label: "A poor season gives less than (kg/ha)"})
shareBelow = d3.rollups(years, v => d3.mean(v, d => d.yield < poor ? 1 : 0), d => d.n, d => d.sow_day)
  .flatMap(([n, rows]) => rows.map(([sow_day, share]) => ({n, sow_day, share, label: `${n} kg N`})))
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 280, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Sowing date", tickFormat: sowLabel, type: "band"},
  y: {label: `Share of seasons below ${poor} kg/ha`, tickFormat: "%", domain: [0, 1], grid: true},
  fx: {label: null, tickFormat: d => `${d} kg N/ha`},
  color: {legend: true, ...nColor},
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(shareBelow, {x: "sow_day", y: "share", fill: "label", fx: "n", inset: 4, tip: true,
      title: d => `Sown ${sowLabel(d.sow_day)}, ${d.n} kg N\n${fmt.pct(d.share)} of 33 seasons below ${poor} kg/ha`})
  ]
}), "niger_poor_years_by_date", "33 seasons per date; area-weighted mean of 132 cells")
```

## Where the date matters most

```{ojs}
cellsN = bestCell.filter(d => d.n === nPick).map(d => ({...d, gain: d.mean - d.mean_jun01}))
modal = d3.rollups(cellsN, v => v.length, d => d.sow_day).sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1])[0]
md`The best fixed date hardly changes across the area: **${sowLabel(modal[0])}** gives the best mean yield
over the 33 seasons in **${modal[1]} of ${cellsN.length}** weather cells (${nPick} kg N). What changes from cell to
cell is how much the date is worth. Moving from 1 June to the cell's best date adds between
**${fmt.int(d3.min(cellsN, d => d.gain))}** and **${fmt.int(d3.max(cellsN, d => d.gain))} kg/ha**, a median of
**${fmt.int(d3.median(cellsN, d => d.gain))} kg/ha**.`
```

```{ojs}
viewof mapMetric = Inputs.radio(new Map([
  ["Gain: best date minus 1 June", "gain"], ["Yield at the best date", "mean"], ["Yield sown on 1 June", "mean_jun01"]]),
  {value: "gain", label: "Map"})
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 460, aspectRatio: 1,
  projection: {type: "equirectangular", domain: cellFeatures(cellsN)},
  color: {scheme: mapMetric === "gain" ? "Greens" : "YlGnBu", legend: true,
          label: {gain: "Grain gained by the best date (kg/ha)", mean: "Mean yield at the best date (kg/ha)",
                  mean_jun01: "Mean yield sown on 1 June (kg/ha)"}[mapMetric]},
  marks: [
    Plot.geo(cellFeatures(cellsN), {fill: d => d.properties[mapMetric], stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.4}),
    ...placeMarks(Plot, adm1, adm2, {labels: "adm2", fontSize: 9}),
    Plot.tip(cellsN, Plot.pointer({x: "lon", y: "lat",
      title: d => `${d.lat.toFixed(2)} N, ${d.lon.toFixed(2)} E\nbest date ${sowLabel(d.sow_day)}: ${fmt.int(d.mean)} kg/ha\n` +
        `sown 1 June: ${fmt.int(d.mean_jun01)} kg/ha\ngain ${fmt.int(d.gain)} kg/ha\nmillet ${fmt.int(d.ha)} ha`})),
    Plot.frame()
  ]
}), "niger_cell_map", `0.1° AgERA5 cells with millet in MapSPAM 2020; mean of 33 seasons, ${nPick} kg N`)
```

## Fertiliser comes second

```{ojs}
gain = d45.map(d => ({sow_day: d.sow_day, gain: d.mean - d0.find(e => e.sow_day === d.sow_day).mean,
                      y0: d0.find(e => e.sow_day === d.sow_day).mean, y45: d.mean}))
gTop = gain.reduce((a, b) => (b.gain > a.gain ? b : a))
md`Forty-five kilograms of nitrogen add **${fmt.int(gTop.gain)} kg/ha** when millet is sown on
${sowLabel(gTop.sow_day)}, and **${fmt.int(gain[0].gain)} kg/ha** when it is sown on 1 June. Nitrogen helps a crop
that has water; it cannot help one that has none. In this model the date sets the ceiling, and fertiliser
only decides how close to it the crop gets.`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 240, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Sowing date", tickFormat: sowLabel, type: "band"},
  y: {label: "Grain from 45 kg N (kg/ha)", grid: true},
  marks: [Plot.barY(gain, {x: "sow_day", y: "gain", fill: "#2b6cb0", inset: 6, tip: true,
            title: d => `Sown ${sowLabel(d.sow_day)}\n0 kg N: ${fmt.int(d.y0)} kg/ha\n45 kg N: ${fmt.int(d.y45)} kg/ha\n` +
              `gain ${fmt.int(d.gain)} kg/ha`}), Plot.ruleY([0])]
}), "niger_n_response_by_date", "mean of 33 seasons: 45 kg N minus 0 kg N")
```

## What this does not say

- **Simulated, not observed.** Why the simulated yields differ from official statistics, in every case study:
  [FAQ](../about/faq.qmd#why-do-the-simulated-yields-differ-from-the-official-statistics).
- **Uncalibrated.** CIVT is the cultivar of a 1986 experiment, at 3 plants/m² and without pests or
  weeds. The level is not a forecast of farm yields: at its best date the simulation gives about twice
  FAOSTAT's national millet yield for Niger, 0.48-0.55 t/ha in 2018-2020 [@faostat_qcl]. The ranking of the
  dates is the result, not the kilograms.
- **No re-sowing.** The model keeps the first crop after a false start; it does not sow again.
- **One date for everyone.** Every cell sows on the same day. A rule that waits for the rains in each cell
  (the onset mode of xdssat, `seasons > mode: per_cell`) is the natural next experiment.
- **Rain from a reanalysis.** AgERA5 June-September rain in these cells was a median 265-307 mm in
  2018-2020; the Sadoré station file of the 1986 experiment has 546 mm for June-September 1986, a different
  year. Station or satellite rain (CHIRPS) is an input away ([Input data](../xdssat/data.qmd)).

## Run it yourself

```bash
python scripts/prepare_weather.py   --config configs/cases/niger-millet.yml
python scripts/prepare_crop_mask.py --config configs/cases/niger-millet.yml
python scripts/prepare_soils.py     --config configs/cases/niger-millet.yml --aoi niger_millet
python scripts/run_aoi.py           --config configs/cases/niger-millet.yml
python docs/scripts/export_cases.py niger
```

The three-year version of this area ships with xdssat: `example-inputs/niger_millet/`
([Examples](../xdssat/examples.qmd)).
